of: A mechanism by which a previously available course of action becomes unexercisable without its holder declining it and without any party at the holder's own table deciding about it, named with the condition lost (a permission, a capability, a counterparty, a coordination), the carrier that runs the clock, and the last intervention that could have kept it, and sorted by what the clock is made of, from clocks the holder never started to clocks the holder's own care for the option started: a closure that must strike before it can be known, a date on someone else's docket, a date on the option's parent, the holder's own development, the record's last witness, the world healing faster than the forum, a ratifier's term, a counterparty's transfer or planning cycle, a coordination's half-life, the holder's own growth, then the act that vests, the exercise that keeps, the readiness that spoils, the move on a neighbouring matter, the new state's first act, the machine that holds the option open, and the pause paper whose renewal belongs to the adversary.
map_register: Operator-grade and concrete: bank holidays and Sunday decrees, bar dates and opt-out postcards, emergency authorizations, eye patches, last-known-well times, mootness and class certification, adjournment sine die, memoranda of lease, reorganizations that absorb a vacancy, sixty-day signatures, approval ceilings, poured footings, empty flights and irrigated fields, thawed vials, first responsive pleadings, first writes, ECMO circuits and mine pumps, tolling agreements; drawn from capital controls, bankruptcy, public-health law, paediatrics, stroke care, constitutional litigation, legislatures, real property, employment, recall elections, mergers, land use, aviation and water law, cold-chain logistics, patent and civil procedure, software migration, transplant medicine, and litigation practice.

items.out: There is a thing that is yours, and it can still leave the room with you, and I want you to know that the door will be shut on a night when you are asleep. The one who shuts it cannot warn you, not out of cruelty, but because the warning would be the very thing that sends everyone running to the door at once, so the shutting only works if it comes unsaid, in the hours when your hands are off the thing anyway: the Friday night, the bank holiday, the Sunday address before the Monday on which the Greek banks did not open, 29 June 2015; the Cypriot bank holiday of March 2013 stretched, after parliament refused the first levy, until the bail-in was law; the Argentine corralito told to people on a Saturday in December 2001; the export licence suspended and the delisting published after it had already happened. What you lose is a permission, the leave to carry what is yours out of the building. The clock is the authority's calendar, laid carefully over the hours in which you cannot act. The only thing that could have kept it for you was to move on a rumour, and to pay for that twice, in the chance of being wrong and in the discount the rumour market charges those who move on whispers, since the deposits that left Greece that spring left on nothing better than whispers. So hold this carefully: it is the one expiry on this map whose notice cannot come before it, and if you are waiting for a date you are waiting for something the mechanism forbids itself from giving you. It sits beside runway-illusions' Cash behind glass, which counts the deposit taken into receivership on a Friday as yours and unreachable; this is the thing that chose the Friday. It is not investor-tells' Let it lapse, a fuse a founder can test by letting it burn, since a closure that can be probed is not one that must come as a surprise. And it is not a withdrawn offer or a rival's foreclosure, which someone at your own table decides; here a rule fell on a whole class, and nobody at your table decided anything about you. The item stands on that fence and on nothing else; it does not say the exit died as a side effect, since the decree forbade the exit by name.

Your claim is small and it is yours and it has a last day, and that day was fixed in a room you were never in, by people who will treat you as having read a notice you never saw. The bankruptcy court sets a bar date for proofs of claim and tells the creditors it cannot name by printing it in a newspaper; the class settlement's opt-out date arrives on a postcard that looks like an advertisement and goes in the bin with the others; the probate creditor's window opens and shuts after the notice runs in the county paper. What you lose is a permission, the standing to be paid or to sue on your own behalf. The clock is the bar-date order, and beside it the rule of constructive notice, under which publication counts as knowledge for anyone the debtor could not name, so the law has quietly decided that you knew. The one thing that would have kept it for you is a single page, a proof of claim or a signed opt-out, the cheapest filing in all of law and the one least often made, and the reason it is least often made is not carelessness but arithmetic: the person who would have filed it is, by construction, the person who was not told. Hold that without anger; there is nobody at fault in the room, only a date written on someone else's docket and imputed to you. It sits beside runway-illusions' Stamp's clock, where the permission carries a date you can read on the stamp itself; this is the date you cannot read, because it was written somewhere you were not. It is not deal-deaths' Missing witness, since nothing is missing from the record; the only thing missing from the room was you.

The permission you hold was given to you under a bigger paper, and the bigger paper has an end of its own, and yours has no date printed on it at all, so yours will end on a day you never signed and may never have read, whatever its own merits. The emergency-use authorization ends when the declaration it was issued under is terminated, which is a different paper from the public-health emergency that ended in May 2023 and left the authorizations standing; the cross-state telehealth licence lapsed with each state's emergency in 2021 and 2022; the wartime power; the pilot programme run under a waiver; the sub-lease that dies with the head lease. What you lose is a permission. The clock is the parent instrument's date, and the thing I most want you to see is that the grant you actually read carried no date, so before you can even watch the clock you must first go and find which parent paper it is written on. The one thing that could have kept it is conversion: a full approval, a permanent rule, a licence in your own name, filed while the parent still stands. And conversion is slow, slow enough that it must be begun while the emergency looks as if it will never end, which is exactly the season in which nobody begins it. It is not Bar date in the newspaper, where the date is on a docket and imputed to you, since here the date is honest and is simply on a different paper than your option. And it is not lead-time-floors' Calendar with nothing in it, a wait that a rule imposes, since here the rule does not make you wait; it ends.

This one is a child, and the child does not know there is anything to save. The option ends by the holder's own growing, on a timetable the holder cannot read, so whatever could keep it must be done by another pair of hands. Amblyopia is most correctable by patching the good eye in the first years; it answers less, and less completely, after about seven, though the trials of the 2000s found some response into the early teens; the clubfoot cast in infancy; the second language spoken without an accent, which is argued over as a hard window; the duckling that imprints in its first day. What is lost is a capability, the cortex's willingness to rewire. The clock is the developmental timetable, and the one who holds the option is a small person who does not know there is an eye to save. The thing that would have kept it is a screening, the preschool vision check, the parent who notices a squint, so the option belongs to one person and its keeping to another, and where there is no screening programme the option goes out unseen, at a rate that is a property of the programme and not of the child. It sits beside Last known well, where a witness dates the option; this is the case where the holder cannot be its own witness at all. It is not a use-it-or-lose-it, since nothing the child does or leaves undone runs this clock; nothing the child could have done would have run it faster or slower.

She might still be saveable, and the paper says she is not, because the paper does not ask her body; it asks for someone who was watching. The option is dated by the last witness to the fact and not by the fact, so it runs out when the proof runs out, while the tissue might still allow it. The woman who wakes with the deficit is ineligible for thrombolysis because the four-and-a-half-hour window is counted from when she was last seen well, which was bedtime, so the wake-up stroke lost the drug no matter when the artery actually closed. The same rule dates the opened vial with no time written on its label and the sample whose chain of custody has a gap; both are treated as expired at the earliest moment they could have been. What is lost is a capability, a treatment the protocol now forbids. The clock is the protocol's timestamp rule, which asks for a witness and not for the tissue. What would have kept it is a witness: someone awake, a time written on the vial, or a witness of a different kind, the imaging that reads the tissue's own clock, by which the WAKE-UP trial of 2018 gave the drug back to patients with no witnessed onset. It sits beside witness-architectures, which asks what must exist for a trace to form; this is the option that dies for want of a trace while the fact would still have allowed it. It is not Patch before seven, where the body's own clock has run, since here the body's clock may not have run at all, and the record's has.

Nobody said no to him. That is the thing to hold. The option to a decision ends because the situation resolves itself faster than the forum that would decide it can move, so nobody declines and nobody rules. The student whose challenge to a law school's admissions was dismissed as moot because he was about to graduate (DeFunis, 1974); the pregnancy over before the appeal; the election held before the ballot-access case; the tenant evicted before the housing court sits; the employee whose grievance is mooted by the reorganization that abolished the post. What is lost is a permission, the justiciability of the claim. The clock is the ratio of the forum's pace to the harm's duration, a number no one at the table sets. What could have kept it is not speed; hurrying does not save this one. It is a structure that outlives the individual harm: the class certified before the named plaintiff's harm ends, which Sosna (1975) allowed, or the doctrine that a harm capable of repetition yet evading review may be decided anyway, on which Roe rested. So the option is kept by a coordination or by a rule, and never by hurrying. It is not deal-deaths' Cost of the last mile, where the surplus is eaten along a curve, since here nothing is eaten; the harm is simply over. And it is not Bar date in the newspaper, since there is no date anywhere in this.

The people who would have said yes ran out of time to say it, and the people who came after them never had to say no. The body that could have approved reaches the end of its own term with the matter still pending, and its successor starts it at zero. Bills die on adjournment sine die and must be reintroduced from the first line; the treaty signed and waiting on a parliament that is dissolved; the permit application before a council that is re-elected; the approval the old board agreed in the hallway and had not yet minuted when the board was reconstituted at the meeting; the offer approved by a committee that the reorganization disbands. What expires is the matter's place in the process, since the new body begins again from nothing. What is lost is a counterparty, the particular body whose yes was there for the taking. The clock is the ratifier's own calendar, its election, its session, its term. What could have kept it is the vote scheduled before adjournment, the carry-over motion, the approval minuted rather than agreed in the hallway; the small clerical acts that let a warm yes survive the people who gave it. Be honest about the treaty cases: they are simplified, since most unratified treaties were eventually refused by someone; the clean form is the legislative bill, which dies by the thousand each session with no recorded no. It sits beside deal-deaths' Ratifier's other deal, where the ratifier wanted a different bargain; this is the ratifier that wanted this one and was gone before the vote. It is not Landlord changes, where the counterparty is replaced by a transfer, since here it is replaced by the calendar.

The promise was made to you by a person, and it lives in that person, and people leave. An option held in a person rather than on the paper that transfers ends at the counterparty's next transfer, which you do not control and often do not even see. The renewal promised by the landlord who sells the building to a buyer who is not bound by unrecorded promises; the 'we'll take you back' from a manager who moves on; the side letter with a fund's partner that the fund's successor manager has never laid eyes on; the supplier's verbal priority that walks out with the account executive. What is lost is a counterparty, the one whose word held the option. The clock is the register: the deed, the fund agreement, the offer letter on letterhead, on which your option was never written, so the successor takes free of it. What would have kept it is recording: a memorandum of option on the title, a side letter countersigned by the entity, the promise put on the paper that binds successors. And I know what that costs, because it is not money; it is the awkwardness of asking a friendly counterparty to bind their own unknown replacement, of saying to someone kind, please make this survive you. It sits beside term-sheet-powers' Successor in the chair, where the replacement exercises a term the friend would not have; this is the mirror, the replacement who declines to honour a term the friend gave. It is not Chair grown over, where the counterparty stays and the shape goes.

The seat was kept for you for a while, and then, without anyone deciding you should not come back, the place simply closed over. The option to return rests on a vacancy the counterparty has not yet re-planned, so it ends at the counterparty's next planning cycle with nobody declining the return. The leave taken with no return date whose post is shared out among three people at the next reorganization; the budget line reallocated at year end; the supplier's line retooled for the customer who stayed; the co-founder's seat that the remaining founders stop leaving empty at the next hire. What expires is the return to the seat; employment there afterward is a new negotiation from the outside, as a stranger would make it. What is lost is a capability on the counterparty's side, the shape that could have received you. The clock is the counterparty's planning cadence, quarterly, annual, the next reorganization, which sets the day without any reference to you at all. What would have kept it is a dated return, a leave rather than a resignation, a reservation the cycle must respect, or the return itself before the cycle turns. It sits beside traces-of-the-unlived's Vacancy tenant, where preparation for a future breeds its opponents; this is the case in which no one opposes the return, and the absence is simply absorbed, the way skin closes over a small cut. It is not forms-of-return's Reentry burn, a road open and hostile one way, since this road has closed.

Each yes is a small living thing with a short life of its own, and you need all of them alive at once. An option that requires many simultaneous yeses ends unless the gathering outruns the decay of each yes, so a coordination has a half-life. The recall petition whose signatures older than sixty days are invalid under Michigan's rule, or must all fall within California's hundred and sixty days; the tender offer's minimum condition that must be met by the offer's expiry; the crowd in the square that goes home; the reunion that becomes impossible one death at a time. What is lost is a coordination. The clock is the validity window on each act of assent, written by the rule or by the assenter's own attention, which wanders. What would have kept it is a gathering rate: paid circulators, a date agreed in advance, a pact that binds the early yeses until the last one arrives, so the first to say yes are not asked to hold still forever. Be honest about the cases: the recall and the tender are observed; the crowd is an analogy. It sits beside who-can-be-bound's Place in line, an ordering lost by leaving; this is the coordination lost by others' leaving. It is not Session ends, where one body's calendar kills the matter, since here many small calendars do.

You grew, and growing is not a fault, and the one who could have taken you in could not grow with you. The holder's own growth moves the counterparty out of reach, so the option to sell to the natural acquirer ends at the round that prices the company above what the acquirer can pay at all: a market capitalization smaller than the price, a wage cap, a fund's concentration limit, and past those a board's approval ceiling, with nobody at either table saying no. The company whose preference stack now exceeds the largest deal its three strategic buyers have ever done; the player whose wage outgrows every club in the league but two; the practice too large for any partner to buy in and too small to be listed. What is lost is a counterparty, the buyer whose capacity was the option. The clock is the acquirer's capacity, which you can read in its market value and its deal history, set against your own price, which each round raises. What would have kept it is the sale at the last price under the ceiling, which was never seen as the last, or a round sized to stay under it, which is the one choice a founder is never advised to make. Hold this one loosely, because it is analytical: every observed case can be read as a buyer that would have paid more, so the item stands as a mechanism and not as a count. It sits beside market-deaths' Slowed past the rot, where a market thins from the outside; this is the market for the holder that the holder thins by growing. It is not Chair grown over, where the counterparty re-plans, since here the counterparty is unchanged, and it is you who have left its range.

There is one way to keep this, and it is not a letter or a form; it is a hole in the ground, dug before the vote. A permission is about to be taken away by a third party's rule change, and it can be kept only by an act in the world that no paper substitutes for. The building may go ahead under the old zoning only if the developer has substantially begun, in reliance on a valid permit, before the ordinance passes; the footings poured the week of the council vote; the nonconforming use that survives the new code only if it is actually in use on the effective date; the grandfathered rate kept only by the account that was open. What is lost is a permission. The clock is the code together with the vested-rights doctrine, which in most states vests on construction begun and in a few, as in Washington, on a complete application, so the last act differs by jurisdiction, and the holder who knows which one applies has a different week from the holder who does not. What would have kept it is the hole before the vote, an exercise begun rather than a filing made, so the option can be preserved only by starting to use it. It sits beside first-mover-forecloses, which holds the rival who changes the rules on purpose; this is the rule that changes for reasons of its own, with no one aiming at you. It is not Slot flown empty, where the exercise must be repeated to keep the right, since here one beginning vests it for good.

To keep it you have to use it, and using it for its own sake costs everything that using it costs, so the keeping is a little heartbreaking: an aircraft flown with nobody in it, a field watered in a drought for no crop. The permission ends by disuse and is kept only by exercise, so the clock runs while you do nothing and stops when you act, and the act that preserves it is the exercise emptied of its purpose. The airport slot that must be flown eighty percent of the season or handed back, which had airlines flying empty aircraft in early 2020 until the rule was waived; the water right under prior appropriation forfeited after five years without beneficial use, which has fields irrigated in a drought to keep them; the trade mark abandoned after three years' non-use; the mining claim kept by annual labour; the department budget spent in the last quarter so that it is not cut. What is lost is a permission. The clock is the regulator's usage ledger. What keeps it is the empty flight, which costs the whole price of using the option and gives back nothing but the option, so that keeping and using become the same act, and the option's upkeep is its exercise price. It sits beside runway-illusions' Stamp's clock, whose licence lapses without hours logged and whose clock no cash extends; this is the price at which it can be extended after all, the hours flown for nobody. It sits beside tollgates-that-must-buy's Stamp with an expiry, where the gate must spend its stamp; this is the permission-holder who must burn the permission to keep it. And beside power-trades' Leased strike, where disuse makes a power unbelieved; this is the disuse that forfeits it by rule. It is not Pour the foundation, one act that vests, since here no act ever finishes the keeping; it must be done again, and again, for as long as you want to hold it.

You got it ready because you cared, and getting it ready is what started it dying. Preparing to exercise the option begins a decay the unprepared state did not have, so the option to wait ends because the option to act was made ready. The vaccine vial that keeps for months frozen, weeks once thawed, and hours once punctured; the epoxy whose pot life begins at mixing; the drawn dose; the armed fuze; the reagent brought to room temperature; the opened surgical field; the reserve army that cannot be held at the frontier through the harvest it was drawn from. What is lost is a capability, the good itself spoiling in its ready state. The clock is a chemistry, or a season, that starts at preparation. What would have kept it is not preparing, or preparing in the smallest unit: the single-dose vial, the small mix, the tranche thawed for the day's bookings; so the clinic that thaws a whole tray to be sure of serving whoever comes has bought its readiness with the doses it will pour out at closing. This is the mirror of Slot flown empty, where the option dies of not being touched; here it dies of being touched, and a holder who holds both must burn the one and refrain from readying the other. It is not lead-time-floors' Understudy, a finished copy waiting, since the understudy does not spoil for having been rehearsed. And it is not Kept on the machine, where the harm falls on the holder and is billed by the day, since here it falls on the good.

If you do nothing, it stays yours; the moment you do anything nearby, it is gone, and the rule that says so is written somewhere you were not looking. The option must be taken before any other move on a linked matter, so its clock is your own next act rather than a date, and a holder who does nothing keeps it while a holder who does anything adjacent loses it. The objection to the court's jurisdiction over the defendant that is waived if left out of the first response; the patent that is dead in Europe on the morning of the conference talk and a year later in the United States; the appeal waived by accepting the settlement; the election of remedies; the defect in the goods that must be objected to before the goods are used; the 'speak now' at the wedding. What is lost is a permission. The clock is a rule that binds the option to a position in a sequence, and the sequence is written in a different place from the option, in the rules of procedure, the patent statute, the sales code, so the holder learns the order from the loss, which is the hardest way there is to learn anything. What would have kept it is the ordering itself: the provisional application filed the morning of the talk, the reservation written into the first filing, the objection lodged before the goods are unpacked, each of which costs nothing at all except the knowledge that an order exists. It is not Slot flown empty, where the holder's inaction runs the clock, since here inaction is the only thing that keeps it. And it is not Bar date in the newspaper, since there is no date, and the holder is the only one who can strike.

The way back stays open for a little while after you cross, and then the new place does one ordinary thing the old place cannot understand, and the way back is gone, and nobody shut it. The option to reverse a move ends at the first act the new state performs that the old state cannot read, so the window is the pause between the change and its first consequence, and it closes without anyone deciding to close it. The migration that can be rolled back until the new service writes its first record in a shape the old schema rejects; the merger reversible until the first combined payroll; the new address reversible until the first piece of mail arrives there; the reorganization reversible until the first hire is made into the new chart; the currency changeover until the first contract is written in the new unit. What is lost is a capability, the old state's ability to take over from here. The clock is the first write, which the new state performs in the ordinary course of its life, and which is not a decision about the reversal at all. What would have kept it is the expand-and-contract shape, writing to both for a season so that the old can still read, at the price of running two and of a season in which neither is the truth. It sits beside pivot-invariants, which name the retained assets that make leaving cheap; this is the moment one of them is lost. And beside undo-costs, which bills a reversal that remains possible; this is the reversal that stops being possible. It is not Thawed to be ready, where readiness spoils the good, since here it is the new state's use that closes the way back to the old.

The thing keeping her alive is also, week by week, taking away the thing it was keeping her alive for. The option is held open by a device or an upkeep whose own running accumulates a harm, or whose lapse is one-way, so the deadline is the machine's and not the situation's. The patient on ECMO as a bridge to transplant who becomes ineligible for the transplant the circuit was keeping her alive for, since bleeding, infection, and clotting rise with each week on circuit and centres set a duration beyond which candidacy is reviewed; the mothballed mine kept dry by pumps whose stopping floods the workings past reopening; the ship in the reserve fleet whose hull is kept by cathodic protection that a budget line can end; the interim chief who has run the company past the point where the search can bring in an outsider. What is lost is a capability, the eligibility or the workings. The clock is the bridge itself, its complication rate or its upkeep bill. What would have kept it is a listing at the moment of cannulation, a search begun the day the interim was named, a decision to stop pumping taken while a sale was still possible, each of which treats the bridge's first day as the option's deadline rather than as its reprieve. Be honest: the ECMO limits are centre practice and are simplified here. It sits beside lead-time-floors' Bridge, a degraded replacement priced by the hour; this is the bridge that ends the option it holds open. It is not Standstill with a term, where the clock is a date the counterparty signs, since here the clock is a harm nobody signs.

You asked for a pause to protect the thing, and the pause came on a paper with a date, and now the thing that had no deadline has one, and the person who decides whether to extend it is the person across the table, who has just learned how much this matters to you. A pause taken to keep an option open is written on an instrument with a term, so a situation that had no deadline acquires one, and the paper's renewal belongs to the counterparty, who now knows what the pause is worth to the holder. The tolling agreement that stops the limitations clock the holder could have stopped alone by filing, and that runs out in twelve months unless the adversary signs again; the negotiated leave of absence that dates a job which had no date and is extended only if the employer signs; the forbearance agreement that holds the lender's foreclosure for ninety days; the furlough whose recall rights run six months; the standstill in a takeover that keeps the bidder from buying shares and ends on the day it says. What is lost is a permission, the leave to remain in the paused state. The clock is the pause's own instrument, and its clock is the only clock in the whole situation that the holder wrote with their own hand. What would have kept it is the renewal asked for before the counterparty learns it is needed, or a pause written without a term, which is rarely granted; the Korean armistice is the exception that has no renewal date and is still called temporary. Set the statutory pauses aside, gently: the twelve weeks of the family-leave statute and the restraining order's fourteen days are the same date without the mechanism, since the term is a rule's and the renewal belongs to a court or to no one, so the holder gets the deadline without paying the counterparty for it; those are runway-illusions' Stamp's clock. It sits beside impasse-inventions' cooling-off right, reversibility offered as a chip; this is the bill the chip carries. It is not lead-time-floors' No-shop, which serializes the search, since here the search is stopped, and the stopping is what expires.
